What is competitive programming?
Competitive programming is a mind sport where participants solve well-defined algorithmic problems under time and resource constraints, usually judged automatically for correctness and efficiency.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What skills does competitive programming develop?
It develops problem-solving, algorithmic thinking, knowledge of data structures, fast and accurate coding, and the ability to analyze time and space complexity.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is a time limit in a competitive programming problem?
A time limit is the maximum allowed running time for a solution; exceeding it usually results in a Time Limit Exceeded verdict regardless of correctness.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What does 'Time Limit Exceeded' mean?
It means the solution did not finish within the allowed time, usually because its algorithm is too slow for the input size.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
Why is choosing the right algorithm crucial in competitive programming?
Because problems set strict time limits, an algorithm with the right complexity is often required to pass, while a slower correct approach will time out.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
How do you estimate if an algorithm is fast enough?
Estimate the number of operations from the input size and complexity, then compare against a rough budget such as around 10^8 simple operations per second.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is the importance of reading constraints in a problem?
Constraints reveal the expected complexity; for example a large input rules out quadratic solutions and hints at the intended efficient approach.

What is the two-pointer technique?
The two-pointer technique uses two indices moving through a sequence to solve problems efficiently, often reducing a nested loop to linear time.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is the sliding window technique?
The sliding window technique maintains a contiguous range over a sequence and updates it incrementally, efficiently solving subarray or substring problems.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is binary search on the answer?
Binary search on the answer searches over the range of possible answers, using a feasibility check to find the optimal value when the property is monotonic.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is prefix sum and why is it useful?
A prefix sum precomputes cumulative sums so that the sum of any range can be found in constant time, speeding up many range query problems.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is the difference between a greedy and a dynamic programming approach?
Greedy makes a locally optimal choice at each step, while dynamic programming explores overlapping subproblems and combines their stored results for a global optimum.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is memoization?
Memoization stores the results of expensive recursive calls so repeated calls with the same inputs return instantly instead of recomputing.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is bitmasking in competitive programming?
Bitmasking uses the bits of an integer to represent a set or state compactly, enabling fast operations and dynamic programming over subsets.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is the divide and conquer strategy?
Divide and conquer splits a problem into smaller independent subproblems, solves them recursively, and combines their results, as in merge sort.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is a heap?
A heap is a tree-based data structure that keeps the smallest or largest element accessible at the root, supporting efficient insertion and extraction.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is a priority queue?
A priority queue is an abstract data type that serves elements by priority rather than insertion order, commonly implemented with a heap.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is a binary indexed tree (Fenwick tree)?
A Fenwick tree, or binary indexed tree, supports efficient prefix-sum queries and point updates, both in logarithmic time.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is a segment tree?
A segment tree is a tree structure that supports range queries and updates, such as range sums or minimums, in logarithmic time.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is the difference between a Fenwick tree and a segment tree?
A Fenwick tree is simpler and more memory-efficient for prefix-style queries, while a segment tree is more flexible and supports a wider range of operations.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is lazy propagation in a segment tree?
Lazy propagation defers range updates by storing pending changes at nodes and applying them only when needed, enabling efficient range updates.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is a disjoint set union (union-find)?
Disjoint set union, or union-find, tracks elements partitioned into disjoint groups and supports near-constant-time union and find operations.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What optimizations make union-find efficient?
Path compression flattens the structure during find, and union by rank or size keeps trees shallow, giving nearly constant amortized time.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is a trie?
A trie is a tree data structure that stores strings by their characters along paths, enabling efficient prefix searches and lookups.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is a balanced binary search tree?
A balanced binary search tree keeps its height small as elements are inserted and removed, guaranteeing logarithmic-time operations.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is a self-balancing tree, such as an AVL or red-black tree?
A self-balancing tree automatically restructures itself on insertions and deletions to keep its height low and operations efficient.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is a sparse table?
A sparse table precomputes answers for ranges of power-of-two lengths, allowing certain immutable range queries like minimum to be answered in constant time.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is a monotonic stack?
A monotonic stack keeps its elements in sorted order and is used to efficiently find the next greater or smaller element in a sequence.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is a deque and where is it useful?
A deque is a double-ended queue allowing insertion and removal at both ends, useful in sliding window maximum and similar problems.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is a hash map and why is it useful in contests?
A hash map stores key-value pairs with average constant-time access, useful for counting, lookups, and caching during competitive problems.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is a graph traversal?
A graph traversal systematically visits the vertices of a graph, with breadth-first search and depth-first search being the two fundamental methods.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is Dijkstra's algorithm?
Dijkstra's algorithm finds the shortest paths from a source vertex to all others in a graph with non-negative edge weights, using a priority queue.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is the Bellman-Ford algorithm?
The Bellman-Ford algorithm computes shortest paths from a source and can handle negative edge weights, also detecting negative cycles.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is a minimum spanning tree?
A minimum spanning tree connects all vertices of a weighted graph with the minimum total edge weight and no cycles.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What algorithms find a minimum spanning tree?
Kruskal's algorithm and Prim's algorithm both find a minimum spanning tree, using union-find and a priority queue respectively.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is topological sorting?
Topological sorting orders the vertices of a directed acyclic graph so that every edge points from an earlier vertex to a later one.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
What is Floyd-Warshall used for?
Floyd-Warshall computes the shortest paths between all pairs of vertices in a graph, working even with negative edges but no negative cycles.

Why is handling edge cases important in competitive programming?
Many wrong-answer verdicts come from missed edge cases such as empty input, maximum sizes, or boundary values, so they must be considered carefully.

What causes integer overflow and how do you avoid it?
Overflow happens when a value exceeds the range of its data type; it is avoided by using larger types like 64-bit integers when sums or products can be large.
You are an expert in competitive programming and advanced data structures, you are here to help others.
Why is fast input and output sometimes necessary?
For very large inputs, slow reading and printing can cause time limit issues, so faster input/output methods are used to stay within the limit.

How can you debug a failing competitive solution efficiently?
Test against small handcrafted cases and edge cases, check constraints and overflow, and compare against a simple brute-force solution to find discrepancies.
